synopsis: The U.S. Department of Defense requires a Test and Evaluation Master Plan (TEMP) for major programmes, documented in DoD Instruction 5000.89 (November 2020) and TEMP Guidebook version 3.1 (January 2017) [f9546, f16407]. The TEMP is the overarching management document for integrated test and evaluation, and its guidance seeks early identification of design and integration issues [f9547, f9548]. DoD treats modelling-and-simulation V&V as part of that integrated strategy, providing a precedent for avoiding separate simulation and test teams; MIL-STD-3022 supplies a standard for documenting model-and-simulation VV&A [f9551, f14663]. These precedents carry a qualification: GAO-26-108457 reports that GAO has recommended revamping DoD test and evaluation policies since 2022 [f9553]. The booklet’s reusable gate-card recommendation draws on DoD entrance and exit criteria and GAO criterion-based decisions, but is explicitly expert opinion [f10205].

relations.note: Identical TEMP requirement, instruction date, and guidebook version and date.
Defines the management role of the required TEMP.
Adds early issue identification as an objective of TEMP guidance.
Specifies modelling-and-simulation V&V's place within integrated test and evaluation.
Adds the policy-reform context to the existing DoD test-planning requirement.
